clue.text: Proposed position for part of prison

parts.note: to position something is to put it in place
taken as written
a ward is a division of a prison or hospital

explanation.surface: Someone suggests where a wing of a jail should go.
explanation.definitionFit: To suggest a candidate or an idea for consideration is to advance it, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Put minor changes to soldier, perhaps — not major

indicators.note: the letters undergo changes, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a soldier is a type of ant, so perhaps flags the example

explanation.surface: Making small alterations for an army private is no big deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldier' is the soldier ant, not an army man.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of little significance is minor rather than major.

clue.text: Cook, say, food for outlaw

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, so another spelling with the same sound is meant

parts.note: a fryer is a cook who fries
tuck is British slang for food, especially sweets for schoolchildren

explanation.surface: A chef, for instance, prepares grub for a fugitive.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin Hood's band of outlaws included the jolly friar of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: He is one of Robin Hood's merry men, the band of outlaws in Sherwood Forest.

clue.text: Brewer's work enjoyed by traditionalists

parts.note: a brewer's product favoured by drinkers who prefer cask-conditioned beer

explanation.definitionFit: Cask beer is championed by traditional drinkers in Britain, the campaign for it being famous.

clue.text: A small tempest, really, leaves disruption in its wake?

definitions.text: A small tempest, really, leaves disruption in its wake?

parts.words: A small tempest, really, leaves disruption in its wake?
parts.note: a storm so small it fits in a vessel that holds tea leaves; leaves puns on tea leaves

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means great fuss over something trivial, literally a tiny tempest in a vessel for tea.

clue.text: Free supply

definitions.meaning: to bring or hand over goods

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to rescue someone and to bring goods to a customer.

clue.text: Security device isn't totally broke?

definitions.meaning: a hinged metal plate that fastens a door or lid over a staple and padlock
split as two words, someone who still holds a penny (P) is not entirely penniless

explanation.surface: A lock that might also describe someone with a coin left in their pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the punning second reading: split it as HAS P, P being a penny in British money.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a fastening used with a padlock to keep doors and gates shut.

clue.text: Like a garden suburb, out of line

parts.note: as means like
Kew is a London suburb famous for its botanical gardens

explanation.surface: Something resembling a leafy suburb is crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not straight or aligned is crooked.

clue.text: Person calling number is this musician's employer

definitions.text: Person calling number is this musician's employer

parts.words: Person calling number is this musician's employer
parts.note: the proverb says that he who pays the musician calls the tune, so the tune-caller pays him

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb about paying the bagpipe player and calling the tune identifies the musician meant.

clue.text: Activist ignited article in plant

indicators.note: the word in tells us the burning-and-article pieces sit inside the herb

parts.note: mint is a garden herb
set alight means lit
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A protester sets fire to something in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a factory in the surface, but it is the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: An aggressive campaigner for a political cause is an activist, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Consult reference books to appear brighter

definitions.meaning: to search for a fact in a dictionary or directory
things improve or seem more promising, as prospects do

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both searching for information and, of prospects, getting better.

clue.text: Fight with volunteers in military society

parts.note: to spar is to box or argue
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Someone joins the reservists to get into a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek city-state was famed for its warrior culture and harsh soldierly discipline.

clue.text: Critic who watches repeats?

definitions.meaning: someone who writes appraisals of books, plays or films
a person who views things again, re-viewing them

explanation.surface: A critic is a person who sits through programmes a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags splitting the word as RE-VIEWER, one who views again.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who assesses new works in print is a critic.

clue.text: Public school a distant prospect for Thomas Gray

definitions.text: a distant prospect for Thomas Gray
definitions.meaning: Gray wrote an ode on a distant prospect of the Thames-side school

explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gray's 1742 poem is Ode on a Distant Prospect of Eton College; in Britain a public school is a private fee-paying one.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the famous fee-paying boarding school near Windsor, in British terms a public school.

clue.text: Language route into universities

indicators.note: the word into puts the road abbreviation inside the pair of university letters

parts.note: U is short for university, so two of them give UU
RD is the abbreviation for road, a route

explanation.surface: A road leading to several campuses.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the official tongue of Pakistan, a member of the class of languages.

clue.text: Move from Nigeria to capital of Malawi, perhaps

definitions.text: Move from Nigeria to capital of Malawi, perhaps

indicators.note: the letters are moved about, so the word signals a rearrangement
the capital, or first letter, of Malawi is taken

explanation.surface: Someone relocates from one African country to the capital of another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move' shuffles NIGERIA, TO and M (the capital of Malawi); the whole clue is also an example of leaving one's country to settle elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving one's homeland to live abroad is exactly what such a relocation is.

clue.text: Old part-time soldiers drill on range

parts.note: to drill recruits is to train them
a band is a range, as in a wavelength or age band

explanation.surface: Elderly reservists practise at a firing range.
explanation.walkthrough: A trainband was a company of citizen militia in 16th and 17th-century England.
explanation.definitionFit: Such companies were militia of citizens trained part-time, now historical.

clue.text: Collection and delivery leading to court contest

parts.note: a basket is a collection, as in a basket of currencies or goods
in cricket a ball is one delivery by the bowler

explanation.surface: Picking up and dropping off goods ends in a legal dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court contest' sounds like a lawsuit but is a game played on a court.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a team sport played on an indoor court, hence a contest there.

clue.text: Term's incomplete without a head instructor

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the incomplete word goes round the pain
the word is left incomplete by losing its last letter

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
in British slang having a head means a headache, so it gives ache

explanation.surface: A school term is unfinished without its principal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a head' is British slang for a headache, as in waking with a head; 'without' is used in its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmaster or tutor is an instructor of pupils.

clue.text: Practical joke on jerk

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
a sharp pull is a jerk

explanation.surface: A prank played on a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' reads as a fool but is a tug.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoax or tease played on someone is a practical joke.

clue.text: Moving protest after beheading is mischievous

indicators.note: beheading removes the first letter, the head of the word

parts.note: a march is a protest made on the move

explanation.surface: Demonstrators who walk out after an execution are being naughty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after beheading' cuts the head, M, from MARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch smile or look is playfully knowing, a synonym of roguish.

clue.text: Single traveller on coach a long time ago

indicators.note: a traveller riding on the coach is carried within it, so the single piece goes inside

parts.note: a stage is short for stagecoach
one is single

explanation.surface: A lone passenger rides a coach in some bygone era.
explanation.walkthrough: A stage was the usual short name for a stagecoach, the horse-drawn public coach.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric period of stone tools stands for the remote past, as in a phrase meaning ages ago.

clue.text: He ruthlessly exploits nurse, for example

definitions.meaning: a swindler or loan ... who preys on others
the nurse is a species of this fish

explanation.surface: A man who takes advantage of a nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: A predatory swindler bears the name of the fish, and the nurse is one such fish.

clue.text: Danish courtier involved in heroics? Not he!

indicators.note: the letters are involved, tangled up, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: the word he, which Not tells us to take away

explanation.surface: A Danish nobleman is no hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not he' takes HE away from the letters of HEROICS; the rest, 'involved in', are rearranged. The courtier is the foppish one in Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the affected courtier in Shakespeare's Hamlet who referees the final duel.

clue.text: Kind of bait used by anglers

definitions.meaning: a maggot of the bluebottle, used by fishermen as bait

explanation.surface: A type of lure that fishermen put on hooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' looks like part of one phrase, but 'Kind' is its own definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means mild-mannered, and is also an old name for a blowfly maggot.

clue.text: A hard worker on the land recovered from scratch

indicators.note: read as re-covered, turned back over, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a serf was a medieval farm labourer tied to the land
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A tough farmhand got better and started again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recovered' is read as re-covered, turned over, so the farm labourer's word is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin again with a clean slate is to start anew.

clue.text: Causes Richard got extremely involved with

definitions.text: Causes Richard got extremely involved with

indicators.note: the letters are tangled up together, signalling a mix
the extremes are the first and last letters of Richard

explanation.surface: The campaigns that King Richard the Lionheart threw himself into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved with' mixes CAUSES and RD (the first and last letters of Richard); the whole clue also describes Richard I's holy wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Campaigns for a cause are so called, and Richard I led one of the medieval holy wars.

clue.text: Recoil from an act of violence

definitions.meaning: the backward jerk of a gun when fired
a blow struck with the foot

explanation.definitionFit: A gun's jolt on firing has this name, as does a blow with the foot.

clue.text: From Europe lad derived flexible way to rise

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the following words

explanation.surface: A young man from the Continent worked out a bendy means of climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across eu(ROPE LAD DER)ived.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing aid made of cords with rungs is flexible, unlike a rigid one.
